title: FactReliabilityScore.v1
description: A deterministic reliability score over a verified FACT (as opposed to SourceReliabilityScore, which scores a source). It rolls up the fact's verification history — how many independent sources confirmed it, how fresh the last verification is, its contradiction history, the authority of its winning source — into a composite the consumption layer can use to decide whether a cached fact is trustworthy enough to serve or must be re-verified first. It is a derived signal, not a fact: served_as_truth is pinned [false]. Same inputs → same score, every run. Deterministic when scored_at is injected.

score_id.description: content-addressed over (fact_key, factors, confirming_source_count); version in metadata, never in the id

fact_key.description: the fact this score is about

factors.description: the per-factor fact-reliability signals (each 0..1); the composite is derived from these

source_authority.description: authority of the winning source (source-of-law high, FAQ low)

freshness.description: how recently the fact was verified relative to its volatility

contradiction_history.description: 1.0 = never contradicted; lower as contradictions accumulate

verification_recency.description: decays as last_verified_at recedes past the refresh horizon

confirming_source_count.description: how many independent sources confirmed this fact (1 is weak unless single_official_source_ok)

winning_authority_rank.description: the authority rank of the source that won reconciliation for this fact

composite_score.description: the derived 0..1 fact-reliability composite (deterministic function of factors)

serve_recommendation.description: what the consumption layer should do — derived from the composite + freshness

served_as_truth.description: pinned false — a reliability score informs serving, it is never itself the served fact

last_verified_at.description: INJECTED epoch seconds of the last verification (no wall-clock)
